decisions.reason: The candidate already has a complete same-message MODIFY moving the panel power-button connector to the main board and routing it from PWRON on J_PWR_SIG pin 4.
The added connector taps the existing PWRON line and does not change any ESP32-S3 GPIO assignment.
The panel power-button connector does not alter the separate charge-status LED interface.
Adding a connector that taps PWRON does not change the selected ESP32-S3 module or part number.
This candidate concerns power-board BOM readiness, while the source adds a connector to the main board and states no BOM-specific change.
The source relies on the already-defined PWRON signal at pin 4 and adds a local main-board tap; it does not change the interboard connector or pinout.
The main-board panel power-button connector does not affect the sensor-board connector fanout.
The source does not change the SPS30 connector, supply, or I2C-mode signals.
Tapping PWRON for a panel button does not alter USB enumeration, flashing, data routing, or the programming-port role.
The panel power-button connector does not change standalone USB power selection or the 3.3V rail.
Message 439 addresses only relocation of the power-button connector; it does not resolve or change DCDC1 voltage regulation.
The PWRON panel-button tap is independent of the GPIO5-controlled 5V boost enable circuit.
